extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners; patent applicants and their attorneys/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Consolidated USPTO form-paragraph guidance for drafting Office actions, requirements, restriction/election procedures, and decisions on petitions to expunge; used by examiners and referenced by applicants when responding. Covers specific paragraph templates, statutory timing, and examiner notes for handling species/election, restriction, supplemental replies, and petitions under 37 CFR 1.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion of Requirement That Accompanies Office Action (¶ 7.125)
rubrics_metrics.description: This requirement is an attachment of the enclosed Office action. A complete reply to the enclosed Office action must include a complete reply to this requirement. The time period for reply to this requirement coincides with the time period for reply to the enclosed Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.105 and appear at the conclusion of any requirement for information that accompanies an Office action. If the requirement for information is mailed without any other Office action, use form paragraph 7.126 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion Of Requirement Mailed Without Any Other Office Action (¶ 7.126)
rubrics_metrics.description: This requirement is subject to the provisions of 37 CFR 1.134, 1.135 and 1.136 and has a shortened statutory period of [1] months. EXTENSIONS OF THIS TIME PERIOD MAY BE GRANTED UNDER 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.105 and used when requirement for information is mailed without any other Office action. The period for reply is ordinarily set for 2 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion of Requirement Mailed Without Any Other Office Action – Accelerated Examination (¶ 7.126.AE)
rubrics_metrics.description: This requirement is subject to 37 CFR 1.134, 1.135 and 1.136 and has a shortened statutory period of TWO (2) MONTHS. This application has been granted special status under the accelerated examination program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) may be granted but filing a petition for extension will remove the application from accelerated examination. Replies must be filed electronically via EFS-Web; non-electronic replies may delay final disposition beyond 12 months. Only for applications filed on or after Aug 25, 2006 that have been granted special status under the accelerated exam program or under 37 CFR 1.102(c)(2) or (d). Not for health/age-based special status or PPH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion of Office Action That Includes Requirement (¶ 7.127)
rubrics_metrics.description: This Office action has an attached requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105. A complete reply to this Office action must include a complete reply to the attached requirement for information. The time period for reply to the attached requirement coincides with the time period for reply to this Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should appear at the end of any Office action that includes an attached requirement for information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Reply Not Approved for Entry (¶ 7.147)
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplemental reply filed on [1] was not entered because supplemental replies are not entered as a matter of right except as provided in 37 CFR 1.111(a)(2)(ii). [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to notify applicant that supplemental reply filed on/after Oct 21, 2004 is not approved for entry. Do not use if supplemental reply has been entered (use PTOL-326 or PTOL-37 as appropriate). Do not use if supplemental reply was filed during period suspended by the Office under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or (c) — such supplemental reply must be entered. In bracket 1 provide date of receipt (per 37 CFR 1.6). In bracket 2 insert reason for non-entry (e.g., 'clearly not limited to placement of the application in condition for allowance').

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Action: Proposed Rejection of Claims Before Appeal Brief (¶ 7.169)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of appeal, the proposed amendment(s) will be entered and the proposed rejection(s) detailed below will be included in the Examiner’s Answer. To be complete, such rejection(s) must be addressed in any brief on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon entry of the amendment(s) for purposes of appeal: 'Claim(s) [1] would be rejected for the reasons set forth in [2] of the final Office action mailed [3].' In bracket 1 identify all new/amended claims grouped together; bracket 2 identify the rejection (paragraph number or statement, e.g., 35 U.S.C. 103 based on A in view of B). Repeat paragraph for each group of claims subject to same rejection. Use when PTOL-303 (Advisory Action form) item 7 has been checked to indicate proposed amendments will be entered upon appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition Under 37 CFR 1.59(b) To Expunge — Decision Held in Abeyance (¶ 7.204)
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a response to a petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b) to expunge information from the application. The decision on the petition will be held in abeyance until allowance of the application or mailing of an Ex parte Quayle action or a Notice of Abandonment, at which time the petition will be decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must state that information is trade secret/proprietary/subject to protective order or was unintentionally submitted and its retention would cause irreparable harm. Petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(g) must be paid. During prosecution the examiner will determine materiality; if not material, information will be removed from the official file. Use abeyance when prosecution on the merits is not closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition Under 37 CFR 1.59(b) — Petition Granted (¶ 7.205)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision on petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b) to expunge information: The petition is granted. The information has been determined to not be material to examination; applicant required to retain expunged material(s) for life of any patent issuing; expunged material removed from official file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Technology Center Director decides only if information was submitted pursuant to MPEP § 724.02 or in an IDS. Petition may not be granted unless application has been allowed or abandoned, or an Ex Parte Quayle action has been mailed. Send to Office of Petitions if information was not submitted pursuant to MPEP § 724.02 or IDS, or if petition requests waiver of 37 CFR 1.59 requirements (accompanying 1.183). In brackets identify the expunged document (author/title). Mail with PTO-90C cover sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition Under 37 CFR 1.59(b) — Petition Dismissed (¶ 7.206)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph heading indicating petition to expunge has been dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow with appropriate concluding form paragraphs (e.g., reasons for dismissal). (Title present; use appropriate concluding paragraph such as 7.208–7.213 to state specific basis.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Expunge — Conclusion: Material to Determination of Patentability (¶ 7.208)
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a decision on the petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b) to expunge information. The petition is dismissed. 'Materiality' is defined as any information which the examiner considers as being important to a determination of patentability of the claims. The petition is deficient because: [8]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If information is considered material to patentability, explain basis for conclusion in bracket 1. A Technology Center Director decides only if submitted pursuant to MPEP § 724.02 or in an IDS. Petition should not be granted until application allowed/abandoned or Ex Parte Quayle action mailed. Send to Office of Petitions in specified circumstances. Identify the document requested to be expunged in bracket 6 (author/title).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Expunge — Conclusion: Information Made Public (¶ 7.209)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusion that the information has been made public. [1]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 provide explanation of basis for conclusion that the information has been made public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Expunge — Conclusion: No Commitment to Retain Information (¶ 7.210)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition does not contain a commitment on the part of petitioner to retain the information to be expunged for the period of any patent with regard to which such information is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow with one or more form paragraphs 7.207–7.213 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Expunge — Conclusion: No Clear Statement of Trade Secret/Unintentional Submission (¶ 7.211)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition does not contain a clear statement that the information requested to be expunged is either: (1) a trade secret, proprietary, and/or subject to a protective order; or (2) was unintentionally submitted and failure to obtain its return would cause irreparable harm to the submitting party or party in interest. [1]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 indicate whether such a statement was provided and, if so, explain why it is not clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Expunge — Conclusion: No Clear Identification of Information to be Expunged (¶ 7.212)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition does not clearly identify the information requested to be expunged. [1]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 explain why the identification is not clear. This form paragraph must be followed with one or more of form paragraphs 7.207–7.213.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Expunge — Lacks Fee (¶ 7.207)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition was not accompanied by the required fee under 37 CFR 1.17(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 explain why the identification of the information requested to be expunged is not clear (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Expunge — No Statement That Petition Is Submitted By/On Behalf Of Party in Interest (¶ 7.213)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition does not contain a statement that the petition is being submitted by, or on behalf of, the party in interest who originally submitted the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use where petitioner fails to assert proper party-in-interest status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers Not Returned, Pro Se (¶ 7.214)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers in an application that has received a filing date pursuant to 37 CFR 1.53 ordinarily will not be returned. If applicant has not preserved copies, the Office will furnish copies at applicant’s expense. See 37 CFR 1.19 for fees and MPEP § 724.05 for petitions to expunge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises pro se filers that original papers usually remain with the Office; copies can be provided for a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of Species; Species Claim(s) Present (¶ 8.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: This application contains claims directed to the following patentably distinct species [1]. Applicant is required under 35 U.S.C. 121 to elect a single disclosed species for prosecution on the merits to which the claims shall be restricted if no generic claim is finally held to be allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the species and reasons they are independent or distinct. Reply to be complete must include (i) an election of a species even if traversed (37 CFR 1.143), and (ii) identification of claims encompassing the elected species. An argument that a claim is allowable or that all claims are generic is nonresponsive unless accompanied by an election. Election may be with or without traverse; to preserve right to petition the election must be with traverse. If traversing on grounds of non-distinctness, submit evidence now or admit on record. If examiner finds one species unpatentable, evidence/admission may be used in a 103 rejection of others. Upon allowance of a generic claim, applicant may seek consideration of additional species per 37 CFR 1.141.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requiring an Election of Species; No Species Claim Present (¶ 8.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are generic to the following disclosed patentably distinct species: [2]. Applicant is required under 35 U.S.C. 121 to elect a single disclosed species or grouping of patentably indistinct species for prosecution on the merits if no generic claim is finally held allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why species are independent/distinct and reasons for search/examination burden. Reply must include election (with/without traverse) and identification of claims encompassing the elected species. Preservation of petition rights requires traverse. If claims added later, indicate which are readable on elected species. If traversing on non-distinctness, submit evidence or admit on record.

rubrics_metrics.name: In Condition for Allowance, Non-elected Claims Withdrawn with Traverse (¶ 8.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: This application is in condition for allowance except for the presence of claim [1] directed to an invention non-elected with traverse in the reply filed on [2]. Applicant is given TWO MONTHS to cancel the noted claims or take other action (37 CFR 1.144). Failure to act will be treated as authorization to cancel noted claims by Examiner’s Amendment and pass the case to issue. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution closed except for the matter noted. Use when non-elected claims remain after traverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election by Original Presentation (¶ 8.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: Newly submitted claim [1] directed to an invention that is independent or distinct from the invention originally claimed for the following reasons: [2]. Since applicant has received an action on the merits for the originally presented invention, that invention has been constructively elected by original presentation for prosecution on the merits. Accordingly, claim [3] withdrawn from consideration as being directed to a non-elected invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when original presentation constructively elects the originally presented invention; provide reasons why new claim is independent/distinct and withdraw non-elected claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Stand Withdrawn With Traverse (¶ 8.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] withdrawn from further consideration pursuant to 37 CFR 1.142(b), as being drawn to a nonelected [2], there being no allowable generic or linking claim. Applicant timely traversed the restriction (election) requirement in the reply filed on [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether withdrawn claim is 'invention' or 'species'. Use when applicant traversed restriction but claim withdrawn nonetheless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Stand Withdrawn Without Traverse (¶ 8.06)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] withdrawn from further consideration pursuant to 37 CFR 1.142(b) as being drawn to a nonelected [2], there being no allowable generic or linking claim. Election was made without traverse in the reply filed on [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when election made without traverse; state withdrawn claim and basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ready for Allowance, Non-elected Claims Withdrawn Without Traverse (¶ 8.07)
rubrics_metrics.description: This application is in condition for allowance except for the presence of claim [1] directed to [2] nonelected without traverse. Accordingly, claim [3] has been canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 insert appropriate wording (an invention/inventions/a species/species). Use when ready for allowance but non-elected claims canceled due to election without traverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction, Additional Groupings (¶ 8.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: [1]. Claim [2], drawn to [3], classified in [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 insert 'invention' or 'species'. Provide classifications (USPC/CPC) in bracket 4 as applicable. Use for identifying additional groupings in a restriction requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction, Two Groupings (¶ 8.08)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction to one of the following inventions is required under 35 U.S.C. 121: I. Claim [1], drawn to [2], classified in [3]. II. Claim [4], drawn to [5], classified [6].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert USPC class/subclass or CPC subclass/main group in brackets 3 and 6 as appropriate. Use to identify two groupings/inventions to be restricted between.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction, Third and Fourth Groupings (¶¶ 8.09–8.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional groupings III (¶ 8.09) and IV (¶ 8.10) for restriction may be listed similarly with claim, drawing and classification information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 insert appropriate roman numeral for further groupings. Provide classification information in designated brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction, Linking Claims (¶ 8.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] link(s) inventions [2] and [3]. The restriction requirement [4] the linked inventions is subject to the nonallowance of the linking claim(s), claim [5]. Upon the indication of allowability of the linking claim(s), the restriction requirement as to the linked inventions shall be withdrawn and any claim(s) depending from or otherwise requiring all the limitations of the allowable linking claim(s) will be rejoined and fully examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert 'between' or 'among' in bracket 4 and the linking claim numbers in bracket 5. Claims that require all limitations of an allowable linking claim will be entered as a matter of right if amendment presented prior to final rejection or allowance. Amendments after final governed by 37 CFR 1.116; after allowance by 37 CFR 1.312. Warn applicant about potential provisional statutory/nonstatutory double patenting for continuation/divisional claims anticipated by allowable linking claim. Where restriction withdrawn, 35 U.S.C. 121 no longer applies (In re Ziegler).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctness — Heading (¶ 8.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventions are independent or distinct, each from the other because: (heading to be followed by factual showing of independence/distinctness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow with one of form paragraphs 8.14–8.20.02 to show independence or distinctness. Provide classification details in bracket as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate–Final Product Distinctness (¶ 8.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions [1] and [2] are related as mutually exclusive species in an intermediate-final product relationship. Distinctness is proven if the intermediate product is useful to make other than the final product and the species are patentably distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when claims presented to both an intermediate and final product (MPEP § 806.05(j)). Provide example of intermediate product utility and conclude restriction with form paragraph 8.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct Products or Distinct Processes (¶ 8.14.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions [1] and [2] are directed to related [3]. The related inventions are distinct if: (1) not capable of use together or can have materially different design/mode/function/effect; (2) do not overlap in scope (mutually exclusive); and (3) are not obvious variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for related product inventions or related process inventions where inventions as claimed are mutually exclusive. If a generic or linking claim is present see MPEP §§ 809–809.03. Explain why inventions are not capable of use together or can differ materially. Conclude restriction with 8.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination–Subcombination Distinctness (¶ 8.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions [1] and [2] are related as combination and subcombination. They are distinct if (1) the combination as claimed does not require the particulars of the subcombination for patentability, and (2) the subcombination has utility by itself or in other combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify limitations of the claimed subcombination not required by the combination, or evidence supporting that conclusion. Suggest separate utility for the subcombination. Conclude restriction with 8.21. Warn about rejoining and double patenting issues; see MPEP § 821.04(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcombinations Usable Together (¶ 8.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions [1] and [2] are related as subcombinations disclosed as usable together in a single combination. Subcombinations are distinct if they do not overlap in scope, are not obvious variants, and at least one subcombination is separately usable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the subcombination and suggest separate utility other than with the other subcombination. Conclude restriction with 8.21. See MPEP § 806.05(d); warn of double patenting for continuation/divisional claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and Apparatus Distinctness (¶ 8.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions [1] and [2] are related as process and apparatus for its practice. They are distinct if either: (1) the process can be practiced by a materially different apparatus or by hand, or (2) the apparatus can be used to practice a materially different process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when claims are presented to both a process and apparatus for its practice (MPEP § 806.05(e)). Provide factual showing (bracket 3) and conclude with paragraph 8.21. Notify applicant that if a product claim is allowable, process claims depending from or requiring all limitations of the patentable product may be rejoined (see form paragraph 8.21.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus and Product Made (¶ 8.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph heading for situations relating to apparatus and product made by the apparatus (text continues beyond chunk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate distinctness/restriction analysis for apparatus vs product-made claims; follow MPEP guidance referenced in subsequent paragraphs.
